title: Interactive Gambling Amendment (Credit Card Ban and Acknowledgement of Losses) Bill 2023
short_title: Interactive Gambling Amendment (Credit Card Ban and Acknowledgement of Losses) Bill 2023

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would reduce problem online gambling by banning credit cards for regulated online gambling and requiring players to acknowledge their losses before wagering.
Operators of regulated interactive wagering services would face criminal and civil penalties for accepting credit card payments from customers in Australia.
A six-month transition period is proposed to allow operators and customers to adjust to the new rules.
changes: Bans the use of credit cards for online gambling through regulated interactive gambling services.
Requires a person to acknowledge their losses for the current financial year before participating in licensed interactive wagering services.
Creates a criminal offence and civil penalty for operators who accept, offer to accept, facilitate or promote credit card payments from customers in Australia.
summary.affected: Operators of regulated interactive gambling services and their customers in Australia.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The member for Mayo introduced the Interactive Gambling Amendment (Credit Card Ban and Acknowledgement of Losses) Bill 2023, which would ban credit card use for online wagering and require betting apps to display a customer's total losses for the financial year before allowing further bets. The bill cites $25 billion in annual losses, excludes lotteries, and is backed by the Alliance for Gambling Reform.
